findings.text: blocking: the landing fragment names `_attempt_end_recorded` as "the new predicate" that stands the guard down, but no `_attempt_end_recorded` exists anywhere in reckon/ or tests/ at the reviewed head c13b40969 (grep returns nothing); the mechanism is the pre-existing `_exit_record_names_attempt` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:528, present unchanged at base 85717297) imported at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1829. A reader verifying the anchor greps a symbol that does not exist, so the evidence record misstates both the name and the novelty of the safeguard it documents.

non-blocking: the negative-control paragraph reports "the four arms fail ... and the two controls still pass (4 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1)", but the negative-control.log it cites in the same sentence records `5 failed, 4 passed in 6.11s` with arm v also among the failures, and the manifest records the same 5/4; the counts are those of the six-test file from before arm v was added and contradict both the log cited and the fragment's own gate sentence naming nine tests.

item_verdicts.diff: VERDICT diff: read commit by commit from 85717297 to c13b40969 across seven commits; four paths changed (+720/-11) — the two modules, the 545-line test file and one evidence fragment; the claim enumeration is a directory glob rather than a bounded range, and the interim-word deferral is a narrow extra term on deferred_outcome at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:688-699.
item_verdicts.done_when: VERDICT done_when: the arm, clock and own-end clauses are asserted by tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py:337-423 (arms i-iv), :426 (the attempt's own end), :453 (claim as the clock) and :523 (two claims, no attempt record); the base arm and the declared mutation are recorded in base-gate-3.log (7 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1) and negative-control.log (5 failed, 4 passed, EXIT=1), each naming its revision and command; the docstring-consistency clause and the ruff-delta clause carry no test and no recorded log.
item_verdicts.goal: VERDICT goal: the goal is to read a resumed attempt's liveness and verdict through its own claim, worker and exit records; reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:501-538 now answers _current_attempt_number with the described pair and reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:81-85 adds the exit-record stand-down, so a just-resumed attempt is dated from its own claim rather than from the coordinator's repaired word.
item_verdicts.manifest: VERDICT manifest: read; status complete, seven commits listed, the tests: line is the literal pytest invocation, and baseline_suite (85717297, base-gate-3.log, exit 1, 7 failure ids) and after_suite (d9f264df8, head-gate.log, exit 0, no failures) each name a log whose last line is a bare EXIT= line.
item_verdicts.write_paths: VERDICT write_paths: the declared scope is reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py, reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py, tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py, the fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted/ and the figures directory; the diff's four changed paths all sit inside that scope and the figures directory is correctly unused.

justifications.durability: Arms i-iv and arm v each redden under the declared mutation (negative-control.log, 5 failed) and arms i-iv redden at the base revision (base-gate-3.log), while the exit-record clause at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:84 is guarded only by tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py:426, which passes at base as well and so is established by reading rather than by a recorded control.
justifications.evidence: The gate could have failed and did — base-gate-3.log records 7 failed against head-gate.log's 70 passed EXIT=0 — but two done_when clauses (the _manifest_carries_no_verdict_yet docstring and the ruff check/format delta) have no test and no log anywhere in the run directory, and the landing fragment's mutation figures contradict the log they cite.
justifications.fit: The new helpers in reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:539-624 follow the surrounding module's idiom — full docstrings, and a deferred import justified by the cycle through reckon/crew/resumption.py:88 — and no name carries a plan, sprint or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The landed change reads the claim and the exit record exactly as the goal states: reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:520-524 takes the higher of the claim and the attempt record, and reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:84 stands the predecessor-report guard down when the exit record names the current attempt.
justifications.reuse: The claim filename is taken from its owner at reckon/crew/resumption.py:305 attempt_claim_path rather than re-spelled, and the claim enumeration has no prior owner in the repository; the earlier duplicate predicate was folded back into the existing _exit_record_names_attempt at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:528.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in the diff (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py, reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py, tests/test_a_resumed_attempt_is_read_through_its_own_records.py, the docs evidence fragment) is inside the declared write paths, and the declared figures directory is left unused.
